items.title: K-8 math: properties of operations (commutative, associative) as verifiable comparison formulas, using FL-8
items.notes: MERGED 2026-08-08T06:03:34Z. All CI green (build macos/windows/ubuntu-latest, CI gate, CI push gate). Reprioritization pass 2026-08-07 (after FL-11/PR #10023 merged, closing out the then-current backlog): ADJ-STDLIB-COVERAGE.md 5.1 names 'operation properties' as a Major Gap for K-2/elementary math, not yet scoped or shipped. Researched fit: a universally-true LAW ('addition is commutative') doesn't naturally fit the 'relate' fact shape (which states a fact about a specific pair of concepts, e.g. deficient_in(tay_sachs, hexosaminidase_a)) or a 'table' (a lookup), but DOES fit FL-8's comparison-formula shape cleanly: compute both sides for a GIVEN instance and confirm/refute equality, citing the general law. Confirmed CmpOp::Eq / EngineCmpOp::Eq already exists and is wired (lower_cmp_op), so `==` in a formula_relation body works today, no new engine work. Scoped as mathematics/operation-properties.adj composing arithmetic.adj's sum/difference (no new formula-stdlib overlap found via grep for commutative/associative/distributive across specs/data -- only incidental comments in average.adj/data-displays.adj about `sum`'s own associative FOLD pattern, not a shipped operation-properties library): addition_is_commutative(addend_one, addend_two) = sum(a,b)==sum(b,a) (always true -- teaches BY demonstration, computing both sides independently rather than asserting); subtraction_is_commutative(minuend, subtrahend) = difference(a,b)==difference(b,a) (true only when a==b -- teaches the CONTRAST, a common early-elementary misconception target, that subtraction is NOT commutative unlike addition); addition_is_associative(a,b,c) = sum(sum(a,b),c)==sum(a,sum(b,c)) (composes sum twice, the same associative fold average.adj's mean_three/data-displays.adj's range_three already establish). Citations WebFetch-verified live before writing: MathWorld Commutative.html ('Two elements x and y of a set S are said to be commutative under a binary operation * if they satisfy x*y=y*x') and Associative.html ('Three elements x, y and z ... x*(y*z)=(x*y)*z'). Pure content PR -- no ADJ-FORMULA-LIBRARIES spec section needed (mirrors wave2-k2-math-cardinality-comparison, not a language-capability PR like FL-8/FL-9/FL-11). Picking this up next.

items.title: K-8 math: spatial composition (composing/decomposing shapes), derived via rule-based inference over cited primitives
items.notes: MERGED 2026-08-10T07:02:25Z. All CI green (build macos/windows/ubuntu-latest x2, CI gate, CI push gate). STANDING PROVENANCE STANDARD CORRECTION 2026-08-08 (see lessons.md and memory adj-provenance-inference-standard): initially reported this item genuinely stuck -- checked 4 MathWorld pages (Hexagon, Diagonal, IsoscelesRightTriangle, Square) and none states a shape-composition fact ('two triangles make a square') as a citable sentence, since a formal reference doesn't bother spelling out something this elementary. The USER corrected the standard: byte provenance does not need to be verbatim/exact -- the goal is HUMAN-AUDITABLE reasoning. It is fine to cite primitive facts and DERIVE a composite conclusion via the engine's `rule` construct (which already exists, tested via medical-rulebook examples, e.g. contraindicated($D) derived from pregnant(present)+pregnancy_excludes($D)), as long as the inference chain stays inspectable (a query's `steps` trail shows the rule's own citation AND each premise fact's citation separately, so a human can independently verify each link and correct a bad one later) -- the same composition discipline `formula`s already use (mean_three cites sum twice, not a single 'mean of three' source). User also authorized `trust consensus` for a well-established but not-directly-source-stated derivation step, not just `trust authoritative`. Prototyped this live (rule combining the ALREADY-SHIPPED quadrilateral_property table with MathWorld Triangulation.html/PolygonDiagonal.html definitions) before committing, confirmed via the CLI that the full audit trail renders correctly (steps: kind=rule then kind=fact, each with its own citation) and that reverse-bind/abstention both work. Shipped `adj-facts-stdlib/geometry/shape-composition.adj`: rule { head: triangle_decomposition_count($Shape, 2) when: quadrilateral_property($Shape, $Property) source '...(honest split of verbatim MathWorld quote + the elementary diagonal-splits-a-quadrilateral-into-two-triangles reasoning built on it)...' locator Triangulation.html trust consensus } -- derives the fact for all 5 already-shipped named quadrilaterals (square/rectangle/rhombus/parallelogram/trapezoid), abstains honestly on a triangle (no diagonal to draw). Deliberately scoped to ONLY the quadrilateral-by-one-diagonal case (n=4 -> 2 triangles), not a general n-sided-polygon (sides-2) formula -- MathWorld states C_(n-3) triangulating diagonals for a convex n-gon but does not spell out the resulting n-2 triangle count, so generalizing further would need its own honest derivation, left for later. FIRST rule-based (not table-only) content in adj-facts-stdlib's history, and the FIRST adj-facts-stdlib-sourced manifest objective ever (all 72 prior objectives were adj-formula-stdlib-only) -- new manifest objective adj.math.k2.spatial_composition uses competency 'infer' (schema already had this value, unused until now) rather than 'recall'/'compute'. DISCOVERED AND FIXED A REAL BUG surfaced by being the first rule-based content: code/scripts/adj_stdlib_report.py's CLAUSE_PATTERNS['rules'] regex was `^\s*rule\s+[a-zA-Z_]` (copied from table/formula/relate's 'keyword then identifier' shape) but the real `rule` grammar is ANONYMOUS (`rule { head: ... }`, no name before the brace) -- so the old regex silently matched zero rule clauses, meaning source_envelope validation would have reported TRUE regardless of whether a rule was actually sourced (a false-negative gap that existed for however long `rule` has been in the grammar, just never exercised until this content). Fixed to `^\s*rule\s*\{`; added 2 regression tests (test_rule_clause_is_recognized_with_no_name_before_the_brace, test_unsourced_rule_clause_reports_missing_source_envelope) pinning both directions. This tooling fix is in code/scripts/adj_stdlib_report.py, NOT adj_stdlib_provenance.py/adj-verify (confirmed these are separate modules; report.py is this loop's own structural-completeness tool already used as its validation gate all session, not the excluded CAS-provenance system). New e2e test facts_shapecomposition_e2e.rs (3 tests: derives-with-audit-trail, runs-backward, abstains-on-non-quadrilateral). Full validation green: 73 objectives valid (was failing with 2 errors before the regex fix), report exit 0, 23 Python unittest passed (21 + 2 new), adj-lang/-cli suite green, clippy clean.
